items.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
items.summary: Hexels are hexagonal surface elements with first-order color fields that enable efficient 3D scene rendering and reconstruction.
items.whyItMatters: They reduce memory and compute costs, making advanced view synthesis feasible on limited hardware.

items.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
items.summary: The paper introduces ThinkWorld, a VLA model that uses human videos to improve robotic manipulation by reinforcing chain-of-dynamics reasoning.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a scalable way to generalize robot actions from diverse human demonstrations.

items.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
items.summary: The article discusses when to apply test‑time adaptation, noting that interventions can help or hurt depending on batch composition and that accuracy alone can mislead.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers need to know how to balance adaptation benefits against risks in real‑world deployments.

items.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
items.summary: Heads of Security uses learned attention gates to separate instruction and data, defending against prompt injection in large language models.
items.whyItMatters: It improves safety of LLMs by preventing malicious instructions from overriding trusted content.

items.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
items.summary: The paper models relational data as a lattice gauge theory, using Wilson loops to verify composed relationships under independent entity coordinate frames.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers see a novel formalism linking graph databases and gauge theory, enabling efficient consistency checks.

items.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
items.summary: KPPax converts Kinetic PreProcessor chemical mechanisms into differentiable, JIT‑compiled JAX code for machine‑learning use.
items.whyItMatters: Enables gradient‑based learning on atmospheric chemistry models, improving integration with modern ML frameworks.

items.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
items.summary: The paper presents a method for robots to reach precise object poses inside their grasp, improving dexterity and safety in complex in-hand manipulation.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it advances autonomous manipulation, enabling safer, more versatile robots for industry and daily life.

items.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
items.summary: GEPA-Curator enhances learning for self‑improving agents by curating failures beyond just rollouts, addressing prompt, harness, and execution weaknesses.
items.whyItMatters: It improves agent reliability and efficiency, crucial for advanced AI deployments.

items.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
items.summary: The article explores whether large language models can autonomously discover new physical laws by detecting unexpected behaviors in a simulated world.
items.whyItMatters: It tests LLMs’ potential for scientific insight and autonomous experimentation, relevant to AI-driven research.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
items.summary: The paper investigates how synthetic environment diversity influences training of large language model agents that use tools for complex tasks, proposing the SynthAPI pipeline.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a method to systematically improve tool‑use agent performance, crucial for building robust AI assistants.

items.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
items.summary: MuonGS studies how relaxed weight-norm control during LLM pretraining affects optimizer performance across the training trajectory.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding norm control can guide better regularization for more efficient, stable language model training.

items.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
items.summary: MSLA reduces self‑attention’s quadratic cost by partitioning sequences into segments, compressing each into separate memory states for efficient long‑sequence modeling.
items.whyItMatters: It enables larger language models to handle longer inputs without prohibitive compute, improving scalability and performance.

items.summary: Language models pretrained on web corpora collected over multiple years learn both general and domain-specific knowledge. items.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
items.summary: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria. On hidden-profile tasks both look attractive, because how widely a fact is held is confounded with whether it helps. We introduce CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates…

items.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
items.summary: Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, language-based reasoning traces do not provide a reliable mechanism for models to revisit relevant visual evidence, leading to visual forgetting and impairing their ability to reason over video content. items.summary: For audio-language models, an answer change after a local sound-event edit can reflect a response to the event's class, sensitivity to waveform rewriting, or both. We compare matched same-class and different-class replacements of a queried event. items.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices
items.summary: Developing on-device image models requires considering practical user needs, task types and device resource constraints. However, existing benchmarks provide limited guidance on identifying capability gaps between on-device models and server-side models. items.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
items.summary: Traffic forecasting requires modeling complex temporal dynamics and the spatial dependencies imposed by road topology.
